Here he attacks the false prophets, as before he had attacked the "princes."<div eID="gen23624" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23625" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make my people err--</hi>knowingly mislead My people by not denouncing their sins as incurring judgment.<div eID="gen23625" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23626" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bite with ... teeth, and cry, Peace--</hi>that is, who, so long as they are supplied with food, promise peace and prosperity in their prophecies.<div eID="gen23626" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23627" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">he that putteth not into their mouths, they ... prepare war against him--</hi>Whenever they are not supplied with food, they foretell war and calamity.<div eID="gen23627" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23628" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">prepare war--</hi>literally, "sanctify war," that is, proclaim it as a holy judgment of God because they are not fed (see on <reference osisRef="Jer.6.4">Jr 6:4</reference>; compare <reference osisRef="Isa.13.3">Is 13:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Joel.1.14">Joe 1:14</reference>). <div eID="gen23628" type="x-p"/>

Darkness is often the image of calamity (<reference osisRef="Isa.8.22">Is 8:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.5.18">Am 5:18</reference>; <reference osisRef="Amos.8.9">8:9</reference>). <div eID="gen23629" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv12750"/><div sID="gen23630" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv12750"/><hi type="bold">7. cover their lips--</hi>The Orientals prided themselves on the moustache and beard ("upper lip," Margin). To cover it, therefore, was a token of shame and sorrow (<reference osisRef="Lev.13.45">Le 13:45</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ezek.24.17">Eze 24:17</reference>, <reference osisRef="Ezek.24.22">22</reference>). "They shall be so ashamed of themselves as not to dare to open their mouths or boast of the name of prophet" [Calvin].<div eID="gen23630" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23631" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">there is no answer of God--</hi>They shall no more profess to have responses from God, being struck dumb with calamities (<reference osisRef="Mic.3.6">Mi 3:6</reference>). <div eID="gen23631" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 7. cover their lips-- The Orientals prided themselves on the moustache and beard ("upper lip," Margin). To cover it, therefore, was a token of shame and sorrow ( Le 13:45 ; Eze 24:17 , 22 ). "They shall be so ashamed of themselves as not to dare to open their mouths or boast of the name of prophet" [Calvin]. there is no answer of God-- They shall no more profess to have responses from God, being struck dumb with calamities ( Mi 3:6 ).

I--</hi>in contrast to the false prophets (<reference osisRef="Mic.3.5">Mi 3:5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Mic.3.7">7</reference>).<div eID="gen23632" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23633" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">full of power--</hi>that which "the Spirit of Jehovah" imparts for the discharge of the prophetical function (<reference osisRef="Luke.1.17">Lu 1:17</reference>; 24:49; <reference osisRef="Acts.1.8">Ac 1:8</reference>).<div eID="gen23633" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23634" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">judgment--</hi>a sense of justice [Maurer]; as opposed to the false prophets' speaking to please men, not from a regard to truth. Or, "judgment" to discern between graver and lighter offenses, and to denounce punishments accordingly [Grotius].<div eID="gen23634" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23635" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">might--</hi>moral intrepidity in speaking the truth at all costs (<reference osisRef="2Tim.1.7">2Ti 1:7</reference>).<div eID="gen23635" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen23636" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">to declare unto Jacob his ... sin--</hi>(<reference osisRef="Isa.58.1">Is 58:1</reference>). Not to flatter the sinner as the false prophets do with promises of peace. <div eID="gen23636" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 8. I-- in contrast to the false prophets ( Mi 3:5 , 7 ). full of power-- that which "the Spirit of Jehovah" imparts for the discharge of the prophetical function ( Lu 1:17 ; 24:49; Ac 1:8 ). judgment-- a sense of justice [Maurer]; as opposed to the false prophets' speaking to please men, not from a regard to truth. Or, "judgment" to discern between graver and lighter offenses, and to denounce punishments accordingly [Grotius]. might-- moral intrepidity in speaking the truth at all costs ( 2Ti 1:7 ). to declare unto Jacob his ... sin-- ( Is 58:1 ). Not to flatter the sinner as the false prophets do with promises of peace.

entries.content_plain: 11. heads thereof-- the princes of Jerusalem. judge for reward-- take bribes as judges ( Mi 7:3 ). priests teach for hire-- It was their duty to teach the law and to decide controversies gratuitously ( Le 10:11 ; De 17:11 ; Mal 2:7; compare Jr 6:13 ; Jude 11). prophets ... divine-- that is, false prophets. Is not the Lord among us?-- namely in the temple ( Is 48:2 ; Jr 7:4 , 8-11 ).
